clue.text: Comment on extremely readable book

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so take only the outermost letters of readable

parts.note: Mark is a book of the Bible, one of the Gospels

explanation.surface: Someone praises a book for being very easy to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'readable', R and E; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing observation is both a comment and a remark: synonyms.

clue.text: Study of automation gives horrible boor twitches

indicators.note: horrible suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of boor are jumbled

parts.note: tics are involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: A course on automated machines makes a rude man fidget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges BOOR into ROBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotics is the engineering discipline of designing automated machines.

clue.text: After St David's Day, period living by the sea

indicators.note: after places the word for period following the date

parts.note: St David's Day, Wales's national day, falls on 1 March, written MAR I
a period is a stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone moves to the coast just after the start of March.
explanation.walkthrough: St David's Day is 1 March, the feast of Wales's patron saint; 1 is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime describes things connected with or near the sea, such as coastal provinces.

clue.text: Girl got a lift

explanation.surface: A young woman hitched a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lift' is not a car ride but an upward movement; someone who got a lift went up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is a girl's name; to have risen or gone up is to have got a lift.

clue.text: Encourage racing boat in China

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage
a shell is a light narrow rowing boat for racing

explanation.surface: A rowing crew is urged on in a race in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is porcelain, not the country, despite its capital letter at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell china is a very thin, delicate kind of porcelain.

clue.text: Delightful place our parents had to give up after a fall

definitions.text: Delightful place our parents had to give up after a fall

parts.words: Delightful place our parents had to give up after a fall
parts.note: our first parents Adam and Eve were expelled from paradise after the Fall, their first sin

explanation.surface: A family loses a lovely home after an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fall' reads as a tumble, but it is the Fall of humankind in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the paradise Adam and Eve were banished from after eating the forbidden fruit.

clue.text: Loose dress for type of race

explanation.surface: A loose-fitting frock suitable for a certain kind of race.
explanation.walkthrough: A sack race is run with both legs inside a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack dress is a loose shapeless gown; a sack race is a children's sports-day event run hopping in bags.

clue.text: I clear off to get something for tea

indicators.note: off suggests something gone bad or awry, so the letters of I clear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clears away so a teatime treat can be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges I CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a cream-filled choux pastry, a cake eaten at afternoon tea.

clue.text: In volume in America, tons of rubbish

indicators.note: in places the letter for tons inside the American unit

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of the volume unit litre

explanation.surface: America's sheer volume of garbage is measured in tons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts T inside LITER, the US spelling of litre.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is discarded waste lying about in public places.

clue.text: Most empty drinking place is French

parts.note: a bar is a place for drinking
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A remark that a French pub is the quietest around.
explanation.definitionFit: Barest means the most bare, the most devoid of contents.

clue.text: One item of jewellery of a pair permitted

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to wear just one of two matching pieces of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is an ornamental band worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Riles partner, breaking piece of office equipment

indicators.note: breaking suggests shattering into pieces, so the letters of riles partner are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone annoys a colleague by smashing a machine in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges RILES PARTNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser printer is an office machine that prints using a laser beam and toner.

clue.text: Carry child, initially exhausted

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of exhausted

explanation.surface: A tired parent lugs a small child around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes E from 'exhausted'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry, especially something heavy.

clue.text: Quiz team may be beaten by metalworker

explanation.surface: A quiz team could be thrashed by a blacksmith.
explanation.walkthrough: A panel beater is a worker who hammers dents out of car bodywork, so a panel is what such a metalworker beats.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiz panel is a team of contestants; a sheet of car bodywork is a panel, hammered by a panel beater.

clue.text: Great penalty

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased with a hefty punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine means excellent or splendid; a fine is a sum paid as a penalty.

clue.text: Swaggering Scotsman goes over house

indicators.note: goes over places the Scotsman above the house in this down entry

parts.note: Mac is a familiar term for a Scotsman, from the common surname prefix

explanation.surface: A cocky Scot looks around a property.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'goes over' means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes aggressively masculine, swaggering behaviour.

clue.text: Appallingly idle around hot city

indicators.note: around makes the jumbled letters enclose the letter for hot
appallingly suggests something done terribly badly, so the letters of idle are rearranged

parts.note: H stands for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Lazy folk loll around in a sweltering city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appallingly' rearranges IDLE into DELI, and 'around' wraps that round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is a major city in northern India, containing the capital New Delhi.

clue.text: Exchange ideas, reviewing CDs?

explanation.surface: Music critics trade opinions while listening to albums.
explanation.walkthrough: Comparing the notes on two CDs would be checking their musical notes against each other; the question mark flags that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To share and discuss views is to compare notes; examining recordings side by side literally compares musical notes.

clue.text: By public transport, I head for work

parts.note: travelling by bus is going by public transport
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Someone takes the bus to get to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland; NESS appears in many British coastal place names. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: One's business is one's occupation or line of work.

clue.text: Learner has to ask secret

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
inner means private or secret, as in inner thoughts

explanation.surface: A trainee needs to request confidential information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice starting out is a learner or beginner: synonyms.

clue.text: Only partly book this meeting room?

definitions.text: Only partly book this meeting room?

parts.words: Only partly book this meeting room?
parts.note: a division of a book is a chapter, and a building is a house, so the meeting room is named for part of a book

explanation.surface: Someone reserves a conference room for only part of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like a verb meaning reserve, but it is a noun: a section of a book is a chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapter house is the building where a cathedral's chapter of clergy meets.

clue.text: Sat around, supplied with bread?

explanation.surface: Someone lounged about once given a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as 'given a loaf'; the question mark marks the invented sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To have loafed is to have idled; a made-up sense is having been given a loaf of bread.

clue.text: Computers can't do such arithmetic? That's mad

explanation.surface: Someone thinks sums machines cannot do are crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mental arithmetic is done in the head, which a computer, lacking a mind, cannot do; the question mark flags the playful claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental arithmetic is done by the brain without aids; colloquially, mental also means crazy.

clue.text: Finished on top

explanation.surface: Something completed and lying uppermost.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is ended or done is over; over also means above or on top of.

clue.text: Cover inside with new cloth

parts.note: to line something is to cover its inside surface

explanation.surface: A box is lined with fresh fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a fabric woven from flax.

clue.text: Fast road held in small car

indicators.note: held means the motorway contains the next word between its letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, a fast road, written MI
taken as written

explanation.surface: A little car is caught up on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the digit 1 becomes the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is a classic small British car.

clue.text: Put money in kitty for scheme

indicators.note: in puts the letter for money inside the pool

parts.note: a pot is a pool of money, a kitty
L stands for pounds, from Latin libra, hence money

explanation.surface: Someone contributes to a shared fund as part of a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link word; L is the pound sign's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a secret plan or scheme.

clue.text: Summon state official at last

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of official

explanation.surface: Finally, a state official is called in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes L from 'official'.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone is to call them.

clue.text: Pointlessness of fellow joining public service

parts.note: a utility is a public service such as water or gas supply

explanation.surface: A man laments how futile it is to work for the gas board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Futility is uselessness, the quality of achieving nothing.

clue.text: Accept one has to deceive

explanation.surface: A person must allow themselves to be fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one has to' is a link: it says one phrase does both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in a lodger is to accept them; to take someone in is to fool or deceive them.

clue.text: Slow, so adroitly replaced

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in different places, so adroitly is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes a slow worker was skilfully substituted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges ADROITLY; 'so' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means tardy, tending to delay.

clue.text: Not so far away from century, miss run

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
to lose a chance is to miss it
R is the abbreviation for run, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A batsman one short of a hundred misses out on a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Closer means nearer, at less distance.
